svg.title: Bearing Delivery Lifecycle process views
svg.desc: Prepared projection of the approved overview, planning, and implementation process diagrams. Not a SysML semantic model. Overview: Five sequential stages across the software development lifecycle: 01 Work Intake, 02 Lifecycle Planning, 03 Owner Authorization Gate, 04 Lifecycle Implementation, and 05 Completed Result and Evidence. A feedback loop returns requested changes from Owner Authorization back to Planning, an aggregate repair loop operates within in-wave implementation, and a correction path returns findings from Lifecycle-completion system validation to the responsible Implementer. Deployment and release remain under separate authority. Planning: Four sequential planning stages mapping plain SDLC activities to Bearing Delivery Lifecycle roles: 01 Intake and Context (Intake, Architectural Alignment, Scope Definition), 02 Architecture and Integration (Planning and Design, Requirements Engineer when applicable, Systems Modeler, Integration Engineer planning), 03 V&V and Synthesis (Planning Test Engineer, Plan Integrator), and 04 Owner Authorization Gate. An iterative triad between Systems Modeler, Integration Engineer planning, and Planning Test Engineer indicates that linear ordering is unsettled. A feedback loop returns requested changes back to the responsible planning role. Implementation: Implementation lifecycle showing two distinct operational zones: Zone A comprises the repeating declared work-unit loop (01 Baseline Input, 02 Work-Unit Realization with distinct Test Implementer, Product Implementer, and Light Implementer roles, 03 In-Wave V&V and Defect Review with ATE and Reviewer, plus an in-wave repair loop). Zone B comprises the distinct Lifecycle-completion gate (04 Lifecycle-Completion System Validation by Integration Engineer execution running once at Lifecycle completion by default, with a correction path back to Implementers) and 05 Closeout and Evidence Handover. Production release remains under separate authority. Systems Modeler Transfer Function: Proposed architecture under Requirements System issue 107 defining F(bound SDoc, owner-approved model decisions, viewpoints, stable IDs, SysML v2 profile, brand profile) -> (SysML v2, HTML). The governed Requirements System transfer-function boundary encapsulates model skeleton construction, tailored SSC-G-101-2023 v1.1 structure and layout rules, native model semantic validation with a closed typed-findings feedback loop, and the SysON/Sirius graphics engine performing automated diagram layout and rendering under agreed style guides and registered brand visual identity. The engine does not invent architecture or grant approval. Outputs are canonical SysML v2 and human-readable HTML views consumed by the Bearing Definition of Done Manifest, preserving canonical SDoc as the requirements authority.

g.title: Systems Modeler Requirements System Transfer Function Detail Diagram
g.desc: Detailed architecture view of the Requirements System transfer function proposed under issue 107. Inputs (bound SDoc candidate, owner-approved model decisions, viewpoints, stable IDs, SysML v2 style profile, and registered brand profile) enter the governed Requirements System transfer function boundary. Inside the boundary, the model skeleton is constructed and tailored SSC-G-101-2023 v1.1 rules applied; native semantic validation performs syntax, semantic, interface, and traceability checks with a closed typed-findings feedback loop; once checks pass, the SysON/Eclipse Sirius graphics engine performs automated diagram layout and rendering under agreed style guides and registered brand visual identity. The engine does not invent architecture or grant approval. Outputs are canonical SysML v2 and human-readable HTML views consumed by the Bearing Definition of Done Manifest.

g.text: Referenced by stable ID, not duplicated
No logo invented or silently substituted
F(bound SDoc, owner decisions, viewpoints, stable IDs, SysML v2 profile, brand profile) -> (SysML v2, HTML)
GOVERNED PIPELINE · ISSUE #107 PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE · CANONICAL SDOC REQUIREMENTS AUTHORITY
SSC-G-101 v1.1 adapted to SysML v2
• Semantic color only; paired w/ shape
Logo & palette to HTML views only
Blocking findings return to model-creator / Systems Modeler · no candidate output emitted
GOVERNED PIPELINE: Style guides & brand profile remain explicit constraints inside the transfer function.

References bound SDoc UIDs by stable ID

Binds proof cases to model elements & views
• SysML v2 is semantic system-model authority
• SysON renders graphics; does not approve
• Branding applied to HTML presentation only
• Release & deploy remain separate owner gate
TRANSFER FUNCTION FLOW: Bound SDoc + Approved Decisions + Viewpoints + Stable IDs + Style & Brand Profiles
-> RS Model Construction -> Semantic Validation (Typed Feedback Loop) -> SysON Graphic Generator Layout & Render -> Canonical SysML v2 + HTML Views -> DoD Manifest
